svg.text: The label moves mostly because knowledge moves. Except for the corals.
anyone reading a Red List change as a change in the animal
whether a category move is a new assessment or a new condition
the coral block is 233 separate declines rather than one
where the category moves, all taxa
7,517 changes across eight distinct Red List states, 2020-3 to 2026-1
The single biggest flow is Data Deficient into Vulnerable and Endangered:
548 species entered threatened status from DD, which is a first real
assessment and not a fall, and 186 left threatened to DD, which is not
safety. IUCN publishes whether a change is genuine or a knowledge correction
— that flag is not in this archive, so this figure cannot make the split and
and the marine subset, by release
one mark per species; vertical position is how many categories it moved
categories gained above the line, lost below
233 of the 351 marine worsenings are hard corals and 273 of them land in the
2024-2 release alone — the Atlantic reassessment after disease and
bleaching, arriving as one decision on one day. Drop the corals and marine
goes from 5:1 worse to 1.7:1. Sharks and rays are the second block, 60
species and spread across releases. The largest marine improvement is the
green turtle, Chelonia mydas, Endangered to Least Concern.
IUCN Red List Darwin Core archives mirrored by GBIF at hosted-datasets.gbif.org/datasets/iucn/, CC-BY, fetched 2026-09-19; nine dated files, of which
two are republications of an earlier version. Fields are located by term from each archive's own meta.xml because threatStatus sits at index 4 in
2020-3 and index 5 in 2026-1. The join key is genus plus specificEpithet: IUCN writes authorship into scientificName and OBIS does not, and joining on
